title: Minimum Array Length After Pair Removals
summary: Given a sorted integer array, you can repeatedly remove pairs of elements where the first is less than the second.
statement: Given a sorted integer array, you can repeatedly remove pairs of elements where the first is less than the second. Determine the shortest possible array length after any number of such operations.
constraints: nums is a nonempty nondecreasing array.
Each operation removes two unequal values, with the smaller chosen before the larger.
hints: Only an overrepresented value can force leftovers beyond parity.
Pair every majority occurrence possible with a different value; otherwise pair all elements except a parity remainder.
Let f be maximum frequency and n the length; return max(n mod 2,2f-n).
If f>n-f, exactly f-(n-f) majority items remain; otherwise distinct-value pairs can consume all items except the unavoidable odd one.
editorial: If f>n-f, exactly f-(n-f) majority items remain; otherwise distinct-value pairs can consume all items except the unavoidable odd one.

tests.explanation: Pairing one with three and two with four removes everything.
Equal values cannot form a removable pair, so both remain.
